text:
sara: FYI hitting a weird duplicate-create flow in the onboarding sample app when we hit transient 502s.
sara: steps: create -> timeout -> client retries -> second create visible in target service.
sara: looks like the idempotency token isn't being preserved across an async replay when auth refresh happens.
matt: ugh. is this the async client only or sync too?
sara: async only so far (uvloop + httpx async). sync client seems fine.
kevin: can you paste the minimal repro?
sara: gist: ```py
# simplified
async with Client(... ) as c:
    await c.post('/items', json={...})
# if the token expires between attempt and replay, auth refresh path seems to mutate headers and we lose x-idempotency-token
```
sara: When token refresh races, the retry logic reconstructs headers but pulls a fresh idempotency token from the header factory rather than reusing the original.
jen: that's nasty. So the replay is treated as a fresh create by the server. Any chance the server is ignoring idempotency header shape?
olivia: server honors header, we can see different tokens in logs (trace id 0xabc).
kevin: hypothesis: our retry wrapper rebuilds Request() and calls auth hook which injects Authorization and also `x-idempotency-token` from a factory that calls `uuid4()` each time. If auth refresh triggers, the hook runs twice and returns new token.
matt: do we have tests that assert idempotency header stability on retries?
jen: not for async. we only added that for sync client.
olivia: this explains why new-users hitting onboarding sample see two items created. Bad DX.
sara: proposal: immutable RequestMetadata captured at first attempt that carries idempotency_token, and retry should reuse it. Also ensure auth refresh doesn't replace unrelated headers.
kevin: agree. implementation options: capture headers on first send, or store idempotency token in the Request object itself and mark as sticky.
matt: extra ask: can we make this behavior opt-in with a deprecation period? I think it's safe to default to reuse tokens, but call it out in changelog.
jen: also we need typing fixes: AsyncClient.__aenter__/__aexit__ are missing typed contextmanager signatures which means mypy can't detect the request wrapper lifetime. Might be why users close sessions prematurely and trigger token refreshes.
kevin: good catch — I'll add explicit AsyncContextManager[AsyncClient] protocol and ensure exports.
olivia: telemetry: can we add an internal debug flag that prints original idempotency token + replay token so we can triage customer cases?
sara: yes pls. short-term we added a deploy-level log in sample app and confirmed problem for 2 customers.
jen: for backoff defaults, we should recommend decorrelated jitter with max retries 4 for create endpoints. That reduces race surface and duplicates.
matt: agree. update docs in onboarding quickstart and add a note in SDK migration guide.
kevin: action items: 1) patch retry to preserve idempotency token (PR) 2) add async test asserting token equality across retries 3) fix typing for AsyncClient context manager 4) add optional debug telemetry + doc note
kevin: I'll own PR 1+2, target EOD tomorrow.
sara: thanks! I'll update the sample app to use the debug flag and add repro script.
olivia: QA — can you add an integration test that simulates token-expiry mid-flight and asserts single create?
jen: will do. also add a short paragraph in release notes about behavior change.
dev-bot: deploy-checklist: linked PRs required - patch-retry-preserve-idempotency (#4012), async-ctx-typing-fix (#4013), onboarding-debug-logs (#4014).
matt: solid. one more idea: add an optional callback in RetryConfig like `on_replay(request, attempt)` so callers can inspect tokens. could help advanced customers.
sara: +1 that would help platform teams debugging.
kevin: adding that to PR scope if time permits, otherwise follow-up.
jen: thanks team — really appreciate the quick sync.
sara: thanks all :heart:
